references.text: The same chapter gives the command to eat unleavened bread for seven days and warns that anyone who eats leavened bread shall be cut off from Israel.
Repeats the command regarding unleavened bread, stating that no leaven shall be found among the Israelites throughout their land.
Reminder to observe the Feast of Unleavened Bread and to eat unleavened bread for seven days.
The command to observe the Feast of Unleavened Bread is repeated, with reference to the month of Abib.
Leviticus describes the Feast of Unleavened Bread, where one must eat unleavened bread for seven days.
Numbers mentions the feast on the fourteenth day of the first month when unleavened bread is to be eaten.
Deuteronomy commands that leavened bread shall not be eaten with the Passover lamb, but unleavened bread for seven days.
Paul uses the image of leaven and unleavened bread typologically, urging believers to celebrate the feast with unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.
Expands Exodus' command with the theological reasoning: unleavened bread as a memorial of the flight from Egypt.
Links the Passover sacrifice's requirement for unleavened bread to the general prohibition against mixing sacrificial blood with leavened bread.
Complementary rules for the Passover meal: 12:9 regulates the preparation of the lamb, while 12:20 regulates the bread.
